# Contentrain AI Documentation

> Contentrain AI is the MIT-licensed open-source toolkit for Contentrain, the content governance ecosystem for teams and AI agents: a 27-tool MCP server (@contentrain/mcp), a CLI (contentrain), shared TypeScript types (@contentrain/types), agent rules and skills (@contentrain/rules, @contentrain/skills), a generated typed query SDK (@contentrain/query), and the open ends of the WordPress migration pipeline (@contentrain/wp-import, @contentrain/emitter-astro, @contentrain/verify). Content lives as canonical JSON/Markdown in your Git repo under .contentrain/ — agents write through deterministic MCP tools, humans review through git branches.

- [Full documentation as a single file (for LLMs)](https://ai.contentrain.io/llms-full.txt)
- [Contentrain Studio (team web surface) documentation](https://docs.contentrain.io/llms.txt)

## Contentrain Products

- [Website](https://contentrain.io)
- [Studio](https://studio.contentrain.io)
- [Migrate, WordPress to Astro migration](https://migrate.contentrain.io)
- [Bridge, free WordPress plugin on WordPress.org](https://wordpress.org/plugins/contentrain-bridge/)
- [Studio docs](https://docs.contentrain.io/llms.txt)
- [GitHub organization](https://github.com/Contentrain)

## Packages (npm)

- [@contentrain/mcp](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/mcp): MCP server: 27 deterministic tools (22 core + 5 media), stdio + HTTP transports, Local / GitHub / GitLab providers
- [contentrain](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/cli): CLI: init, import, serve (review UI + MCP transports), validate, generate, diff, merge, reconcile, prune, studio commands
- [@contentrain/query](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/sdk): universal query SDK; `contentrain generate` emits a typed client into .contentrain/client/ (#contentrain imports); optional CDN transport plus public forms/comments clients
- [@contentrain/types](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/types): shared contract: model/field/config/provider types, the migration contracts (RawIR, ProjectIR, CapabilityManifest, MigrationHandoff), plus pure, browser-safe validate/serialize functions
- [@contentrain/rules](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/rules): always-loaded agent guardrails plus shared quality rules
- [@contentrain/skills](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/skills): 16 on-demand Agent Skills (Agent Skills standard) and 9 framework guides
- [@contentrain/wp-import](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/wp-import): WordPress WXR/REST importers → RawIR → .contentrain content store
- [@contentrain/emitter-astro](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/emitter-astro): ProjectIR → a complete Astro project, returned as a pure file map
- [@contentrain/verify](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/verify): offline SEO/indexing/link/asset gates for a built site; takes documents, never makes a network request
- [@contentrain/astro-kit](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/astro-kit): copy-in Astro components for Contentrain sites, with a machine-readable catalog
- [@contentrain/decide](https://ai.contentrain.io/packages/decide): small typed decisions (a choice or a score): rule first, then a model, cached, budgeted and audited

## Claude Code plugin

- contentrain (marketplace Contentrain/ai, not npm) — the MCP server, 7 core skills and 9 framework guides in one install: /plugin marketplace add Contentrain/ai

## Key Facts

- 4 model kinds: collection (object-map by entry id), singleton, dictionary (flat string map), document (markdown + frontmatter)
- Every model declares title_field: the field shown as an entry's title. Must be a string/text/slug/email/url/code/markdown/richtext field on that model; dictionaries use the reserved "key". Required — `contentrain validate --fix` backfills it in older projects
- 27 field types; content is validated before every write — an error on any entry in a contentrain_content_save call means nothing is committed
- The MCP tool registry holds 27 tools, but `tools/list` is filtered per session: a tool whose requirements (local project root, provider capabilities, a media stack) cannot be met is never registered. A local stdio server lists the 22 core tools; media tools appear only on media-capable providers such as Studio MCP Cloud
- Every write lands on an isolated cr/* git branch; workflow is auto-merge or review (config.json)
- dry_run previews: contentrain_apply and contentrain_reconcile default to dry_run: true, contentrain_bulk takes an optional dry_run; destructive tools (content/model/media/vocabulary delete, merge, branch delete, bulk delete_entries) require confirm: true
- Locale strategies: file / suffix / directory / none; entry status and scheduling live in .contentrain/meta/, not in content
- When a change lands on the base branch directly, the branches diverge: writes still succeed but report base_advance "blocked_diverged". contentrain_reconcile / `contentrain reconcile` is a content-aware three-way merge (field, dictionary key, term+locale granularity) with a closed 9-value conflict code set
- WordPress migration chain: wp-import → RawIR → [migration engine, CLOSED SOURCE] → ProjectIR → emitter-astro → verify. The MIT packages are the two ends and the contracts; the analysis that produces a ProjectIR is not in this repository and these packages do not convert a site on their own
- MIT licensed, local-first (no cloud dependency); GitHub/GitLab remote providers are optional peer dependencies
